column1: # AQL Language Specification: module fn-VALUE application boundary
# Format: input<TAB>expected<TAB>description
# Boundary rows for a module-captured Function VALUE applied inside its
# own module — the execFnDefSig same-registry dispatch class routed onto
# the main-tape splice branch (the TCO-STAGED Stage-5 residual flip; see
# design/SUB-ENGINE-MAIN-TAPE-REVIEW.0.md R2). The shape needs VALUE
# dispatch, so the callee is an ANONYMOUS fn in the export map (a named
# module fn resolves through its registered body-runner handler instead)
# and the caller takes it via an UNNAMED Function param, splicing the raw
# value onto the body frame. Every row pins behaviour that held on BOTH
# sides of the flip — the def-cleanup / error / flow boundary must not
# move.
# The VALUE-result twins (application result, module-scope resolution,
# args.N, composition) live in lang/go/native/fnvalue_sameregistry_test.go
# rather than here: a module fn with an UNNAMED Function param currently
# COMPILES to a unit that misses the runtime auto-dispatch (the
# interpreter returns the dispatch result; the compiled unit returns 0
# values), so value rows of this shape would trip the compiled
# differential on a pre-existing compiler gap, not on the boundary under
# test. Top-level fns of the same shape now REFUSE compilation (the
# "unnamed fn-value param auto-dispatches on the body frame" guard in
# eng/go/carrier.go::runFnBodyOnce); extending that refusal to the
# module-fn unit path is the open follow-up recorded in
# design/SUB-ENGINE-MAIN-TAPE-REVIEW.0.md §7.
# §1  the frame tears down — nothing leaks
import module [def useanon fn [[Function Integer] [Integer] []] export "L" {useanon: useanon/r, lk: (fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [def tmpz 7 x add tmpz]])}] end L.useanon L.lk 1 end tmpz
column3: a body-local def is torn down by the frame tail — it must NOT leak past the call

column1: # §2  errors and flow control cross (or refuse to cross) the boundary unchanged
import module [def useanon fn [[Function Integer] [Integer] [(args.0 args.1)]] export "L" {useanon: useanon/r, bm: (fn [[x:Integer] [Integer] [raise oops_e "bang"]])}] end L.useanon L.bm 1
column3: a raise inside the value-dispatched body propagates out as the same error (the args body makes the caller REFUSE compilation via the unnamed-fn-value guard, so the row runs interpreted; the raise fires on the frame auto-dispatch)

column1: import module [def looper fn [[Function] [Integer] [def acc 0 for 5 [def acc (acc add 1) (args.0 1)] acc]] export "L" {looper: looper/r, brk: (fn [[x:Integer] [Any] [break]])}] end L.looper L.brk
column3: a break in a value-dispatched body does not escape the module-call boundary

column1: import module [def looper fn [[Function] [Integer] [def acc 0 for 5 [(args.0 1) def acc (acc add 1)] acc]] export "L" {looper: looper/r, skp: (fn [[x:Integer] [Any] [continue]])}] end L.looper L.skp
column3: a continue in a value-dispatched body does not escape the module-call boundary
